subjects.name: Police militarization in the United States

summary: The closing Behind the Police episode traces how US police became militarized, from the Texas Rangers' ethnic cleansing and Smedley Butler's Prohibition-era Philadelphia force to SWAT raids, the drug war and the 1985 MOVE bombing.

evidence.note: Texas Rangers introduced, officially formed 1835; earliest period covered at length
Rangers in the Comanche Wars and the 1840 massacre of a Comanche village
Rangers kill hundreds of ethnic Mexicans 1915-1919; sealed legislative hearing
Butler appointed Philadelphia public safety director to enforce Prohibition militarily
Cold War Office of Public Safety trains foreign police; trainers later return to US forces
Watts uprising of 1965 framed as the inciting moment for modern militarized policing
origins and actual use of SWAT teams, mostly drug search warrants
Dragnet, Cops and procedurals shaping public belief in police effectiveness
1985 MOVE bombing on Osage Avenue as the closing case study
2020 cancellation of Cops and Live PD after George Floyd's murder; covered span ends 2020

notes: Survey episode with no single bastard; primary subject modelled as a practice. main_span starts at the 1965 Watts uprising, when the episode says modern militarization took off; Rangers (from 1835) and Butler (1924-1925) are earlier precursors in covered_span. Cold War police training abroad (VN, IR, UY, AR, BR, CO) got only a few minutes, so setting is US only. Transcript garbles some years (Butler '1942', MOVE '1905'); 1924 and 1985 used.
